question: A company with a small network team purchases 10 Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches for a network refresh. Some elements of the existing network infrastructure will be retained including DHCP and DNS servers. The company wants the network team to use PowerOn Auto Provisioning (POAP) to configure the switches, but the team only has experience with manual configuration. Which two additional network infrastructure components must be configured to use POAP? (Choose two.)
theory: Beyond the DHCP and DNS infrastructure the company already has, POAP still needs a TFTP server to host the configuration script the switch downloads during bootstrap, plus a file repository (commonly reached via SCP) holding the actual software image and configuration files the script installs — these two additions complete POAP's documented network requirements. A NETBOOT/PXE-style discovery service, a GIT server, or an SNMP trap receiver play no role in POAP's bootstrap chain. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
